newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels parade strength, vow to kill Mobutu.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels parade strength, vow to kill Mobutu.

text.p: Hundreds of newly trained recruits joined the ranks of Laurent Kabilas rebel army on Wednesday, vowing to fight until they killed Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko.
In the third such parade in rebel-held eastern Zaire within a week, more than 500 new rebel fighters paraded through the streets of this town on the shores of Lake Tanganyika bordering on Burundi.
"Our struggle will continue until Mobutu is killed," sang the rebels, wearing U.S.-style combat uniforms, wellington boots and carrying rifles. They lauded Kabila in other war songs.
Hundreds of residents took to the streets of Uvira and danced in joy behind the latest members of Kabilas Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (AFDL).
The ceremony following parades of some 1,200 newly trained recruits in Bukavu on Tuesday and 5,000 in Goma last Thursday was part of a well-organised campaign to show off the alliances strength.
Kabila told a rally his forces were advancing on several fronts after capturing the northeast town of Isiro on Tuesday.
"The advance will continue until our objective is met. We must move forward and defeat Mobutus army," Kabila added.
Kabila said Isiro fell to a multi-pronged rebel advance against one of Africas most ill-disciplined armies, which even with mercenary help has failed to turn the tide.
Kabila said government troops and some of the 300 foreign mercenaries hired by Kinshasa had retreated to Buta, the next stop on the road towards Mobutus jungle palace at Gbadolite in northern Zaire.

The Zairean army said on Wednesday it was fighting to defend the northeastern town of Isiro but it was seriously threatened. It admitted the fall of Bafwasende, 230 km (140 miles) northeast of Kisangani, the headquarters for an army counter-offensive.
A senior defence ministry official said a cargo plane loaded with Ugandan troops to fight alongside the rebels crashed inside Zaires border in the Ruwenzori mountain area and some aboard were killed.

The official, saying Zairean troops took survivors prisoner, presented the crash as evidence of direct Ugandan involvement in the fighting -- a charge Kinshasa has also levelled at Rwanda and Burundi.
All three countries have denied the Zairean accusations.
France, which has long supported Mobutu, said on Wednesday Kabilas rebels would be excluded from an international conference which Paris wants organised on the Zaire crisis.

"This is a conference to be attended by states and which is to be organised by the United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity ," foreign ministry spokesman Yves Doutriaux told reporters who asked him if the rebels would be invited.
Doutriaux was replying to questions about a statement in Paris on Tuesday by Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni, who said he did not believe a conference would bring a quick solution to the crisis.
Paris suspects the Ugandan government, with U.S. acquiescence, of aiding and abetting the Rwandan-backed rebels.
